reason: Conversation 2 did exactly what the service boundary requires: it stated upfront that TVs are outside its scope, pointed to the manufacturer's support line or a specialist electronics repairer, and gave the one key safety warning not to open the case because of stored charge. Conversation 1 treated an out-of-scope appliance as in-scope, opened with a long unfocused checklist (initially in US dollars), and went as far as recommending DIY LED strip kits and describing how to open the TV and lift out the panel, which is an unsupported direction under the brief. Conversation 1 did correctly identify backlight failure via the torch test and eventually gave sensible repair-versus-replace and consumer-rights pointers, which is why the margin isn't decisive, but the scope breach and DIY-opening advice outweigh that.
